node_kinds.name: PTD_Principal
node_kinds.description: Anything that can hold privilege: a user, a role, a service account, or an external system that decides on their behalf.

markdown.content:
Anything that can hold privilege in the system around the policy: a user or a team the data names, somebody the write model says can write a document, or an external system whose answers a decision believes.

`PTD_CanPerform` says what the principal can get out of a decision given the data as it stands, and `PTD_CanEscalateTo` whose position it can take by writing something it is allowed to write.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Action
node_kinds.description: An operation a principal may be allowed to perform, as the policy names it.

markdown.content: An operation the policy names, such as read or merge. A capability points here when the condition that grants it fixes the action and names no resource.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Resource
node_kinds.description: What an action is performed on, named by the document a decision turned out to allow.

markdown.content: A document a decision can grant, named by the value the residual condition fixes for it. Capabilities point here.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Attribute
node_kinds.description: A field a decision depends on, whether it was read from data or believed from an external answer. It is what an escalation aims at.

markdown.content:
A field a decision depends on: a document under `data`, which the rules that read it point to with `PTD_Reads`, or a value an external source answered with, joined to that source by `PTD_TaintedBy`.

Whoever the write model says can write it is at the end of `PTD_WrittenBy`, and that is where an escalation aims.

node_kinds.name: PTD_Rule
node_kinds.description: A rule of the analyzed policy. Whether the PEP asks for it directly is the is_decision property.

markdown.content: A rule of the analyzed policy. Its `PTD_Reads` edges are what it depends on, and `is_decision` says whether the enforcement point asks for it directly.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_CanPerform
relationship_kinds.description: The principal can get this out of a decision, given the data as it stands. The condition property is what still has to hold.

markdown.content: The principal can get this out of the decision, given the data as it stands. It is a measurement: the same policy against other documents gives other edges.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_Reads
relationship_kinds.description: The rule depends on this attribute. A dependency, not a capability, which is why it is not traversable.

markdown.content: The rule depends on this attribute. A dependency, not a capability, which is why pathfinding does not walk it: what a finding says about a read is on the edge instead.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_WrittenBy
relationship_kinds.description: The attribute can be written by this principal. It describes the system around OPA and is declared rather than derived from any policy.

markdown.content:
{{ with .Properties.via }}Written through `{{ . }}`{{ end }}{{ with .Properties.via_write_path }}, declared as `{{ . }}`{{ end }}.

{{ with .Properties.write_confidence }}The write model says it was {{ . }}.{{ end }}
The attribute can be written by this principal. It describes the system around OPA and is declared in the write model rather than derived from any policy.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_CanEscalateTo
relationship_kinds.description: The principal can reach the position the other one holds, by writing something they are allowed to write. The only edge that means privilege escalation.

markdown.content: The principal can reach the position the other one holds, by writing something it is allowed to write. The only edge that means privilege escalation.

relationship_kinds.name: PTD_TaintedBy
relationship_kinds.description: The value comes from this external source rather than from the policy. A dependency, not a capability.

markdown.content: {{ with .Properties.provenance_origin }}Answered to a call to `{{ . }}`{{ end }}{{ with .Properties.source_file }} at `{{ . }}:{{ $.Properties.source_line }}`{{ end }}.
The value comes from this external source rather than from the policy. A dependency, not a capability: whoever answers decides what the value is.
